candidates.title: Efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants approved for cardiovascular indications: Systematic review and meta-analysis.

C1_OPEN_LICENCE.evidence: Europe PMC licence cc by, PMC5967718

C2_RCT_ONLY.evidence: We used data from Phase 3 randomized trials that compared an FDA-approved DOAC with VKA for primary prevention of stroke in patients with NVAF or for treatment of acute VTE.

C3_POPULATION.evidence: In the five Phase 3 studies of DOACs for acute treatment of patients with a DVT, with or without pulmonary embolism (PE), participants randomized to receive a DOAC did not differ from those receiving warfarin on the odds of recurrent VTE and related death

C4_INTERVENTION_VS_COMPARATOR.evidence: FDA-approved direct oral anticoagulants versus warfarin for treatment of VTE.

C5_OUTCOME_AND_ESTIMAND.evidence: In the five Phase 3 studies of DOACs for acute treatment of patients with a DVT, with or without pulmonary embolism (PE), participants randomized to receive a DOAC did not differ from those receiving warfarin on the odds of recurrent VTE and related death (the primary outcome in most studies of secondary prevention in acute VTE), but this primary outcome showed a tendency to favor DOACs (OR 0.88, CI 0.75–1.03).
